title: The unique normalized integral pullback tower comparison
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and a scheme morphism f:X → Y, with independent site and coefficient universes. Let R_W be the completed integral coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let f* be the ordinary module pullback along the unique completed coefficient map compatible with every finite quotient [lem-tw-completed-coefficient-ringed-coherence]. There is a unique natural isomorphism of whole strict towers from the global quotient reduction tower of f*P to the recorded tower Res_n f_n*(P tensor_(R_Y) S_(Y,n)) [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-a1-integral-finite-pullback-tower, def-pur-integral-finite-pullback, def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. It is natural in every unbounded cochain complex P. In degree i over the inverse-image object of V in Y.ProEt, its nth component sends a tensor unit_f(x) to a times unit_(f_n)(1 tensor x), for every finite coefficient section a and every section x of P^i over V. No invertibility of l on X or Y, completeness, boundedness or constructibility assumption is required.

proof.text: The completed coefficient map is the transpose of the projection-compatible map in lem-tw-completed-coefficient-ringed-coherence. Apply the ring-sheaf adjunction naturality equivalence to transport every projection equation and its uniqueness. This gives exactly the original ambient coefficient map, direct image and its ordinary left adjoint, with independent site and coefficient universes.

For each quotient n, the projection square gives a sectionwise identity isomorphism between restriction followed by completed direct image and finite direct image followed by restriction. The normalized scalar-reduction adjunction and the completed and finite pullback adjunctions show that pullback followed by reduction and reduction followed by finite pullback are left adjoints to this same functor. Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq gives their canonical isomorphism. Its unit equation is the claimed formula on unit-coefficient generators. Finite linearity and the scalar-extension generator smul formula give every coefficient.

Completed coefficient projections are locally surjective. Hence a map between restrictions of finite modules is uniquely a finite-linear map, using IntegralScalarProof.liftMap. The composite pullback/reduction hom equivalence is injective: equality after the composite unit implies equality of the original maps. Apply this to degreewise maps and the recorded generator formulas for unrestricted reduction and finite pullback transitions. Both transition composites take the composite unit to the same finite pullback of the reduced section, so they agree.

Lift the finite comparison to cochain complexes and restrict to completed coefficients. NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles the compatible comparisons, and pointwise invertibility gives a natural isomorphism of the whole strict towers. Use the proved equality of the global slice tower and unrestricted tower. A normalized competing isomorphism agrees on the composite units; the preceding injectivity, followed by chain-map, tower-map and natural-transformation extensionality, proves uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem pullTowerModel {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃! b : pullTower l E f ≅ integralOperationsPullbackTowerFunctor l E f,
      ∀ (P : CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E Y) ℤ) (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ)
        (V : Y.ProEt) (a : (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E X n).obj.obj
          (op ((Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))) (x : (P.X i).val.obj (op V)),
        (((b.hom.app P).app (op n)).f i).val.app
            (op ((Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V))
          (IntegralOnSlice.generator l E X none n ((pull l E f).obj (P.X i))
            (op ((Scheme.proEtaleBaseChange f).obj V)) a (pullSection l E f (P.X i) V x)) =
          finitePullSection l E f n P i V a x
